surprises.description: FY2027 EPS growth guidance of low double digits to low teens is below the preview’s $15.02 consensus, which implied roughly 13.7–14% growth. The outlook therefore came in softer than the analyst benchmark, even though the preview had allowed for a low-to-mid-teens guide.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management guided FY2027 adjusted EPS growth to “low double digits to low teens.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2027 EPS (the real event)” consensus was “$15.02” and “+13.7–14%”; the preview’s base scenario described an EPS guide of “low-to-mid-teens.”

surprises.description: Client incentives rose 21% in Q4, higher than the preview’s expectation of growth only slightly above Q3’s 18% and above the level it flagged as a warning sign. Management also expects a larger share of payments volume to renew in 2027, implying continued incentive pressure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Client incentives grew 21% in Q4, a step-up of nearly 3 points from Q3,” and “about 25% of payments volume” is expected to renew in 2027 versus 20% in 2026, “implying further incentive growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Q4 client incentives were guided to grow “slightly above Q3’s +18%” and that “anything meaningfully north of +20%” would reframe the pricing-power story.

surprises.description: Visa’s FY2027 value-added services growth guide of low-to-mid 20s is weaker than the FY2026 growth rate of 30% and reaches or falls below the preview’s roughly 25% concern threshold. That tempers the expectation that VAS would continue to offset pressure elsewhere.
surprises.fact_evidence: VAS grew 30% in constant dollars to $14 billion in FY2026, while management guided to “low- to mid-20s% VAS growth in 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Deceleration below ~25% would undercut the core bull case” and that the bull case required VAS to “hold[] >30%.”

surprises.description: The $3.48 Q4 EPS beat the $3.44 consensus, but it was below the preview’s derived $3.52–$3.54 whisper bar and the beat was driven primarily by a lower tax rate from legal-settlement tax benefits. The headline beat was therefore smaller and more tax-dependent than the preview’s higher bar implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q4 EPS was “$3.48,” beating expectations “primarily due to a lower-than-expected tax rate of 18.4%, driven by claim-of-right tax benefits from legal settlements.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed non-GAAP EPS consensus of “$3.44” and derived a buy-side bar “nearer $3.52–3.54.”

surprises.description: Management said Q2 FY2027 will be the growth low point because of tough comparisons, adding a weak quarter to the expected growth cadence that the preview had not identified. This is a new near-term caution even alongside the full-year growth guide.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management expects “Q2 to be the growth low point due to tough comparisons.”

surprises.description: The dividend increase was larger than the preview’s 10–14% base case: Visa raised its quarterly dividend by 16%.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s dividend-raise base case was “10–14%.”

surprises.description: Visa disclosed that stablecoin settlement had reached a $25 billion annualized run rate, up 10x year over year, alongside substantial card-program and partner pipelines. That is more concrete scale and adoption than the preview’s expectation that stablecoins might remain limited to qualitative commentary and a few use cases.
surprises.fact_evidence: Stablecoin settlement “surpassed $25 billion in annualized volume, up 10x year-over-year”; stablecoin-linked card programs exceeded 225, with over 5 million cards, and the platform pipeline had over 300 partners.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said settlement volume or named client adoption could be a “narrative unlock,” while “another quarter of qualitative framing” would confirm stablecoins were not yet a 2027 earnings driver.

surprises.description: Visa received Chinese central-bank approval to begin formal preparations for domestic processing in Mainland China, a material strategic development that the preview did not flag. The approval starts preparations rather than indicating that processing has begun.
surprises.fact_evidence: Visa received “People’s Bank of China approval to prepare for domestic processing,” beginning formal preparations to ultimately process on the Visa network in Mainland China.
